amendments.rule: Reordered or discontinuous target tokens may occupy one unit when they realize one source item. Do not absorb unrelated intervening words into that unit. **Where English repeats one source function word because its scope is distributed across coordinated or emphatically repeated phrases, every English occurrence belongs to that source morpheme's one possibly discontinuous unit.** `מִן` in `מִבּוֹא בְדָמִים וְהוֹשֵׁעַ` → *from bloodguiltiness, and from avenging* takes both occurrences of *from*, while the waw takes only *and*; `בִּי אֲנִי` → *upon me ... upon me* gives both occurrences of *upon* to the single preposition while the suffix and explicit pronoun take their respective *me*. The repeated English word is neither `added` nor reassigned to a neighboring source item merely to make the units contiguous. **An explicit personal pronoun is read the same way where the ASV resumes it in a later clause of the same verse.** Where a following verbless clause writes no subject of its own and the ASV supplies the subject pronoun that an explicit `הוּא`, `הֵמָּה`, `אֲנִי` or the like standing earlier in the verse denotes, both occurrences belong to that pronoun's one discontinuous unit, exactly as rule 18 gives both pronouns of a twice-rendered suffix to the suffix and rule 20 gives both halves of an identifying formula to its one `הוּא`: `הֵמָּה סֹחֲרֵי יָדֵךְ ... בָּם סֹחֲרָיִךְ` → *they were the merchants of thy hand ... in these were* ***they*** *thy merchants* gives both *they*s to the one `הֵמָּה`, headed on the first. Such a pronoun is not `added`, and it does not join the predicate's unit: rule 20 hands the predicate the construction's copula and, in a presentative clause, its dummy *there*, and a referential pronoun is neither, so the clause's supplied *were* goes to the predicate while the pronoun goes to the morpheme that denotes it. This governs a clause with no subject of its own: where a finite verb stands in the resumed clause it takes the English subject pronoun under rule 17, which is a pronoun realizing that verb's own person and number.
amendments.why: Rule 25's distribution sentence is written for a 'source function word', which left no clause for an explicit pronoun the ASV resumes in a later verbless clause. EZK.27.21's verse pass fell into that gap and folded the resumed 'they' into the predicate participle as a supplied copular frame, so the omission is demonstrably actionable rather than theoretical. The widening is carried by two clauses the contract already has - rule 18 on a suffix the ASV's paraphrase realizes twice, and rule 20 on an identifying formula that realizes one pronoun as both subject demonstrative and predicate determiner - so it contradicts nothing. It is deliberately confined to pronouns and says nothing about a copula the ASV supplies for a coordinated or gapped line, which rules 34 and 49 already govern and which EZK.27.11 resolves the other way under rule 8; widening the sentence to verbs would have put this contract at odds with itself.

conventions: The trading formula natan plus a bare object: where the ASV writes a single 'for' and it stands before the verb's own Hebrew object, that word belongs to the verb's unit under rule 44 (27:12, 13, 14, 17, 22), and a be standing on the commodity phrase the ASV renders bare is unrepresented under rule 40 (27:13, 17). Where the ASV writes a preposition before the be's own phrase as well, each morpheme takes the word standing before its phrase (27:12, 16, 19, 22). Rule 44's limit about 'a preposition of the object's own' reaches a preposition on the object itself and not any preposition elsewhere in the clause, so count the ASV's prepositions against the morphemes that could carry them and read which phrase each stands before.

arav plus ma'arav is decided by MACULA's form, not by the English. The construct participle 'orvei ma'aravekh (27:27) is a construct chain, so 'the dealers in thy merchandise' puts the 'in' on the rectum under rule 19; the infinitive construct la'arov ma'aravekh (27:9) takes an accusative object, so 'to deal in thy merchandise' keeps the 'in' with the verb under rule 44. Same English preposition, two analyses, and the verbal form is what separates them.

machaziqei bedeq is rendered by the single English word 'calkers', so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the participle and bedeq share one unit headed on the participle, in both 27:9 and 27:27. The suffix stays outside the fusion and takes its own 'thy', since dropping that word loses the suffix's own rendering. The earlier reading, which left bedeq unrepresented beside the rendered participle and cited rule 22, was corrected in both verses.

Where the ASV realizes one source item twice, both occurrences stay with that item. 27:21's resumed 'they' belongs to the one hemmah (rules 18, 20, 25), and 27:11's doubled 'were' to the one hayu that governs both coordinated clauses. On 27:11 the competing reading, which treats the first clause as gapped and puts its supplied copula on the preposition heading the prepositional predicate under rules 34 and 49, is recorded on the unit; the distributed reading was taken because the verb is actually written in that sentence.

report: Checked all 48 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket but one is the ASV rendering one morpheme differently in contexts the source licenses: the 2fs suffix's thy/thee/of-thee split tracks possessive vs object vs nomen rectum (rules 18, 19), and the varied renderings of the prepositions and of kol and rav are each the word the ASV wrote.

One real split, in the treatment of a source item the ASV realizes twice. 27:11 gives both occurrences of 'were' to the single hayu governing the two coordinated clauses (rule 25), naming the gapped-copula alternative under rules 34 and 49 on that unit. 27:21 instead handed the resumed 'they' of 'in these were they thy merchants' to the predicate participle as a construction-supplied copular frame. Rule 20 gives a predicate the copula and a presentative dummy and nothing further; 'they' is referential, and the morpheme it denotes (hemmah) stands written earlier in the same verse. Patched 27:21 so both 'they's belong to hemmah in one discontinuous unit, the supplied 'were' staying on the predicate. 27:11 is left as accepted: its reading is defensible and the competing one is already recorded under rule 8.

Because the candidate table is blind to added units, I read the dump end to end for supplied English handled two ways. The two italic 'and's (27:23 between Asshur and Chilmad, 27:29 before the second kol) are the chapter's only surplus coordinators; counting waws against ASV 'and's across all 36 verses, they agree everywhere else, including 27:27, where five waws answer four 'and's and the surplus waw is unrepresented. Supplied 'the', 'of', 'with' and 'in' go in every verse to the noun that determines them or whose case-function licenses them (rules 15, 33). The added 'saying' (27:32) and 'their' (27:35) answer to no morpheme.

27:31's two supplied reflexives were examined and left as accepted. 'themselves' stays with the Hiphil hiqrichu under rule 44's clause on a pronoun rendering the verb's own voice or elative sense, which names the Hiphil expressly; the Qal chageru has no such licence, so its 'them' is added under the same rule's main clause. The difference is in the stem, which is in the source, so this is not a split.

The trade formula was checked in all seven natan clauses. Where the ASV's single 'for' stands before the verb's own bare Hebrew object it belongs to the verb (rule 44: 27:12, 13, 14, 17, 22), and a be on a commodity phrase the ASV renders bare is unrepresented (rule 40: 27:13, 17). Where the ASV writes a preposition before that phrase too, each morpheme takes the word standing before its own phrase (27:12, 16, 19, 22). Consistent throughout.

arav plus ma'arav is analysed two ways for the same English string, and the source licenses it: the construct participle of 27:27 is a construct chain, so 'in thy merchandise' puts the 'in' on the rectum (rule 19), while the infinitive construct of 27:9 takes an accusative object, so 'deal in' keeps the 'in' with the verb (rule 44). Recorded as a convention.

BSB: none of the five listed disagreements is an error. All are documented convention differences - rule 27's lamed of le'mor, rule 40's recast prepositions in 27:5, 8, 13, 17, 30, rule 41's determiner limit at 27:26, the adonai suffix at 27:3, and 27:27's waw, whose competing margin reading 'and in' is already recorded on the unit. Nothing was changed to move the aggregate.

One amendment, to rule 25. Its distribution sentence is written for a 'source function word', which left a resumed subject pronoun uncovered; that gap is what the 27:21 unit fell into. The amendment names the case and carves out rule 17's finite verb. It says nothing about copulas, so it neither collides with rules 34 and 49 nor unsettles 27:11.
